label: Computing the Trifocal Tensor
notes: Chapter 15 told us what the trifocal tensor does; this chapter, spanning printed pages 391 to 408, asks how to estimate one from image data. The shift is computational: a valid tensor is supported by trilinear equations, has a stable nullspace, normalizes sensibly, and produces small reprojection residuals on real triplets.

label: Trilinear Equations
notes: Each point-point-point correspondence over three views contributes four linearly independent trilinear equations in the twenty-seven entries of the tensor. Stacking these gives a homogeneous system A t equals zero. Line correspondences supply two equations each, so points and lines mix freely to build the design matrix.

label: Minimum Data
notes: The tensor has twenty-six degrees of freedom up to scale but only eighteen are geometrically independent. Seven point correspondences give twenty-eight equations, enough to solve linearly. Mixtures count too: a point is worth four equations, a line two, so six points and four lines also suffice for the linear estimate.

label: The Linear Algorithm
notes: With more than the minimum data the system is overdetermined, so we seek the unit vector minimizing the algebraic residual. The singular value decomposition of the design matrix delivers it: the right singular vector for the smallest singular value is the least-squares nullspace estimate, reshaped into a three by three by three array.

label: Why Normalize
notes: Raw pixel coordinates make some rows of the design matrix vastly larger than others, so the algebraic minimum no longer tracks the geometric one. Hartley normalization translates each image so points are centred and scales them to mean distance root two from the origin, equalizing the rows before the null vector is chosen.

label: Normalized Linear Pipeline
notes: The standard recipe is four stages: normalize each view with a similarity transform, solve the homogeneous system for the raw tensor, enforce the internal constraints to make it valid, then denormalize. In the notebook normalization cut the effective condition number by roughly twentyfold without changing the underlying equations.

label: Internal Constraints
notes: A generic twenty-seven entry array is not a trifocal tensor. The valid tensors form an eighteen degree of freedom manifold, so the linear solution must be projected onto it. Each correlation slice has rank two, and the three left and right null vectors are constrained, encoding consistency with three genuine cameras.

label: Parametrization via Epipoles
notes: The clean way to enforce validity is to parametrize the tensor by the two epipoles in the second and third views plus a linear part. Given the epipoles the remaining entries are linear, so an iterative scheme alternates between solving that linear problem and updating the epipoles, guaranteeing a geometrically valid result.

label: Algebraic vs Geometric Error
notes: Algebraic error is the residual of the linear equations: cheap, but not what we ultimately care about. Geometric error is reprojection error, the distance in pixels between measured and predicted image points. The linear estimate minimizes algebraic error and serves as the initializer for the geometric refinement.

label: Gold Standard Estimate
notes: The gold-standard method assumes Gaussian measurement noise and minimizes total reprojection error over the cameras consistent with the tensor, using Levenberg-Marquardt. The transfer residual landscape sampled in the notebook shows a clean basin whose minimum sits exactly at the correct correspondence, the picture motivating Sampson and full geometric refinement.

label: Robust Estimation
notes: Real correspondence sets contain mismatches. RANSAC samples minimal sets of seven points, estimates a tensor, and counts inliers whose transfer residual stays below a threshold. The notebook corrupts four triplets and shows their residuals jump by orders of magnitude, exactly the separation that lets robust voting reject outliers.

label: The Estimation Recipe
notes: Putting it together: interest points across three views, RANSAC to discard outliers, normalized linear estimation for an initializer, constraint enforcement for validity, then the gold-standard reprojection minimization. Each stage in the notebook has a numerical check beside it, from the isolated nullspace gap to the near-zero scaled tensor error.
